source.note: The Moon in the sixth, eighth or twelfth from the lagna and aspected by a malefic: the child dies soon. The verse adds that a benefic's aspect in the same figure leaves it living to about eight, which is a grading the SDK does not model.
A benefic retrograde in the sixth, eighth or twelfth and aspected by a malefic, the lagna unoccupied by a benefic: death within a month of birth.
Saturn, Mars and the Sun together in the fifth: the early death of the mother and of a brother.
Mars in the lagna or the eighth, conjunct Saturn or the Sun or aspected by a malefic, and with no benefic's aspect: a source of immediate death.
Saturn and Mars both aspecting the lagna while the Sun and the Moon join Rahu elsewhere: the child lives only a fortnight.
Saturn in the tenth, the Moon in the sixth and Mars in the seventh: immediate death of the child along with its mother.
Saturn in the lagna, the Moon in the eighth and Jupiter in the third: immediate death.
The Sun in the ninth, Mars in the seventh, and Jupiter and Venus in the eleventh: a month of life.

Any graha in the twelfth is a source of short life, and the Sun, the Moon, Venus and Rahu especially; the aspect of one of those four on the twelfth counteracts it, which this rule requires to be absent.
Saturn in the twelfth, the Sun in the ninth and Mars in the eighth, with no benefic's aspect on them: instant death.
A malefic in the seventh while the waning Moon stands in the lagna: early death. The verse also reads the malefic in the rising decanate, which needs the drekkana of the lagna and is not built here.

All the grahas in the apoklimas, the third, sixth, ninth and twelfth, and bereft of strength: a life of six months or two. The seven are read, since the nodes carry no strength to lack; the verse's two spans are not an outcome, because it names both. Read in the Sanskrit of the 1899 and 1923 prints, which agree (their verse 22 of the chapter).
The mother incurs evils when three malefics aspect the Moon at birth; benefics aspecting her bring the mother good instead, which this rule requires to be absent.
Rahu, Mercury, Venus, the Sun and Saturn occupying the second: the birth followed the father's death, and the mother too faces an early end.

The Moon in the seventh or eighth from a malefic and joined by one, with strong malefics aspecting her: the birth destroys the mother. A malefic the Moon is seventh from stands seventh from her, and one she is eighth from stands sixth; one strong malefic's aspect is read for the verse's plural. Read in the Sanskrit of the 1899 and 1923 prints, which agree (their verse 25 of the chapter).
The Sun exalted or debilitated in the seventh: the child is not raised on its mother's milk.
A malefic in the fourth from the Moon and in a sign of its enemy, with no benefic in a kendra: the child loses its mother prematurely.
Malefics in the sixth and the twelfth bring evils to the mother; the same verse gives the fourth and tenth for the father.
Mercury in the second while malefics hold the lagna, the seventh and the twelfth: the yoga destroys the whole family.
Jupiter in the lagna, Saturn in the second and Rahu in the third: the mother dies early.
A malefic in a trine from the waning Moon and joined by no benefic: the mother gives the child up.
Mars and Saturn together in a kendra from the Moon and in one navamsha: two mothers, and a short life even so.
Jupiter in the lagna while Saturn, the Sun, Mars and Mercury stand together in the second: the father is lost at the native's marriage.
The Sun with a malefic or hemmed between malefics while another malefic stands in the seventh from him: early loss of the father.
The Sun in the seventh, Mars in the tenth and Rahu in the twelfth: the father is unlikely to be sustained.
Mars in the tenth in a sign of his enemy: the father's early death, and the verse says doubtlessly.
The Moon in the sixth, Saturn in the lagna and Mars in the seventh: no long span for the father.
The Sun aspected by Saturn and standing in the navamsha of Aries or Scorpio: the father had left the family or died before the birth.
Malefics holding the fourth, the tenth and the twelfth: both parents leave the child to its own fate.
Rahu and Jupiter together in the lagna or the fourth, in a sign inimical to them: the father does not see the native until the native's twenty-third year.

The Sun indicates the father: malefics aspecting him or hemming him bring the father evils. The same verses read the Moon for the mother. The verses close by asking that the occupants' strength be estimated, a weighing the verses do not reduce to a condition, so this rule answers broadly: it is the principle, not a graded reading.

Malefics in the sixth, eighth or fourth from the Sun bring the father inauspicious results. The verses close by asking that the occupants' strength be estimated, a weighing the verses do not reduce to a condition, so this rule answers broadly: it is the principle, not a graded reading.

The Moon indicates the mother: malefics aspecting her or hemming her bring the mother evils. The verses close by asking that the occupants' strength be estimated, a weighing the verses do not reduce to a condition, so this rule answers broadly: it is the principle, not a graded reading.

Malefics in the sixth, eighth or fourth from the Moon are adverse for the mother. The verses close by asking that the occupants' strength be estimated, a weighing the verses do not reduce to a condition, so this rule answers broadly: it is the principle, not a graded reading.

Mercury, Jupiter or Venus in a kendra from the lagna destroys all the evils, as the Sun eliminates darkness. The antidotes stand in their own chapter, so they ship as rules of their own, which every evil names as a cancellation.
A strong Jupiter alone in the lagna destroys the whole mass of evils, as devotion to Shiva destroys sin. Read in the Sanskrit of the 1899 and 1923 prints, which agree (their verse 45 of the chapter).
The lagna lord alone, strong and in a kendra, destroys every evil, as Shiva destroyed Tripura. Read in the Sanskrit of the 1899 and 1923 prints, which agree (their verse 46 of the chapter).

A benefic aspecting the lagna of a night birth in the bright half, or a malefic aspecting the lagna of a day birth in the dark half, destroys all the evils. It needs the chart to say whether the birth was by day.

Malefics surrounded by benefics while the kendras and trikonas are themselves benefic-occupied: the evils disappear soon, and do not follow from those bhavas. This rule reads the second half, benefics in the kendras and trikonas.
Mars joined by Jupiter or aspected by him is auspicious for the mother as well as for the native.
